deep.reconstruction:
This is a crossed-out draft page (large green X) from Grothendieck's 1983-84 notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', that is, arrangements of pseudolines in a real projective or 2-dimensional setting, treated combinatorially and cellularly. The page belongs to a technical construction step, apparently labelled a), b), c) and then α), β). It modifies a pseudoline system near a family of distinguished curves D_i in a modified surface X̃. The tilde suggests a blow-up or cut-open version of the plane.

(1) Top left. After a case distinction, Grothendieck lists the possible local pictures near a distinguished line, drawn in brown or green, bounded on both sides by yellow lines. The red pseudolines of the system either cross the strip transversally or form small digon or lens shapes inside it. The dashed boundaries of a neighbourhood are marked 'au choix': one may choose where the boundary of the neighbourhood runs.

(2) Item c), partly struck out. One takes a neighbourhood C, probably a 'couloir' (corridor), described in terms of cells or cocells around the subcomplex K_0. He notes he had already used this device to construct an object 𝒢 near K_0. The face F is then replaced by C, and its interior F° by the interior of F∩C. The large bottom-left grid shows several such corridors along successive coloured distinguished lines (brown, green, brown), with the red pseudolines crossing or forming lenses.

(3) NB. These corridors are, 'in the suitable topological category', tubular neighbourhoods of the D_i in X̃. This is an explicit appeal to a tame/PL-type category in which tubular neighbourhoods of 1-dimensional strata in a surface exist and are unique.

(4) α). For the exceptional faces F* adjacent to K_{D_i}, the system Σ, weakened by the choice of the D_i, is 'rectified'. One keeps the part of F* lying above a 'principal frontier' δ and makes the 'usual modifications' near critical points. The heptagon figure shows a face with red pseudolines entering through its sides; below a horizontal line, the lines are straightened into vertical segments ending on a black base edge. This is a local 'sweep' or wiring-diagram normal form.

(5) β). A self-correction. Because of the rectification b), one may no longer characterise the exceptional lines of K as those containing no vertex of L. That property still implies exceptionality, but exceptional lines may now contain several vertices. A struck-out alternative characterisation via unions of cocells is replaced by another: the connected components of K̃ (or of the complement of K') that have no global boundary. The page ends by saying this suggests naturally introducing a further datum.

Overall purpose: a normalisation or rectification lemma. It puts a pseudoline arrangement into a standard form near chosen curves and exceptional faces, in a tame topological category, as part of a larger classification or structure theory of pseudoline systems.
errors: No mathematical error is detectable; the page is too fragmentary for real verification. Item β) is itself Grothendieck's correction of an earlier characterisation of exceptional lines, which the rectification step b) invalidates. The whole page is crossed out, so it is a superseded draft.

ideas.what: Replacing faces by corridor-shaped (cocellular) neighbourhoods of distinguished curves D_i, identified with tubular neighbourhoods in a suitable tame topological category.
ideas.modern_name: Regular/tubular neighbourhoods in PL or o-minimal (tame) topology; regular neighbourhoods of subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (regular neighbourhoods, 1939); PL topology (Zeeman, Hudson); tame topology program
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (topologie modérée) calls for such a tame category in general terms, not this construction.

ideas.what: Local rectification of a pseudoline system inside a face above a 'principal frontier', with standard modifications at critical points.
ideas.modern_name: Sweeping / wiring-diagram normal form for pseudoline arrangements; topological sweep
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman (1980, wiring diagrams); Goodman–Pollack (sweeping, 1980s); Edelsbrunner–Guibas (topological sweep, 1986)

ideas.what: Characterisation of 'exceptional' lines or faces: no vertices of L versus components without global boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Unclear; possibly related to simple/extremal pseudolines or boundary-free components of a cell complex

missed.claim: Grothendieck's pseudoline project sets up a combinatorial-topological normalisation of pseudoline systems near distinguished curves, framed in a 'suitable topological category'. This is a concrete testbed for the tame-topology programme of the Esquisse. The project is unpublished, but this page alone contains only routine technical steps of that construction.
missed.quote: sont (dans la catégorie topologique convenable) des voisinages tubulaires des D_i dans X̃
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of mild historical interest: it documents Grothendieck applying his tame-topology viewpoint to pseudoline arrangements and oriented matroids of rank 3. Nothing new mathematically is identifiable on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a crossed-out technical draft step: tubular-neighbourhood corridors, local rectification of faces, and a self-correction about exceptional lines. These are standard moves in the topological combinatorics of pseudoline arrangements. Only the broader context of Grothendieck's unpublished pseudoline project has historical interest.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'un [tour de] couloir rectiligne(?) convexe' rather than 'en termes de cocellules (convexes'. The word looks like 'couloir' (corridor).
'cf l'avais utilisé' should be 'cf. je l'avais utilisé'.
'F^0[?] ... au[?] ... F∩C' should probably read 'F° par l'intérieur de F∩C'.
'NB Ce contour est ...' is more likely 'NB Ces couloirs sont', continuing onto the next line '(dans la catégorie topologique convenable) des voisinages tubulaires des D_i dans X̃'.
The marginal insertion at top right reads '{F* adjacente à K_{D_i}}'.
'c'est vrai que elles peuvent' should probably be 'c'est vrai, mais elles peuvent en contenir plusieurs !'.
'chose indiquant fort naturel...' is probably followed by '... ensuite la donnée d'...', i.e. introducing a further datum.
The 'ℰ' after 'voisinage ouvert' is likely the letter C, the corridor that later replaces F.
